we can reconstruct a 3D model of a human face from a single 2D image with a high quality, if the initial 3D shape is given.

(i) the proposed quality measure is a useful tool to judge the quality of 3D reconstructions; (ii) the combination method improves the reconstruction results; and (iii) the complete processing pipeline can automatically generate 3D reconstruc-tions with a high quality from a large number of single images of a person.
In summary, our research is concerned with

quality measures for 3D reconstruction from images, with the combination of multiple reconstructions, with the reconstruction from single images and with the combination of these three aspects in a complete processing pipeline.
quality measures for 3D face reconstruction from multiple images and their application to automated face modeling from image databases.
the question how the quality of 3D reconstructions from multiple images can be judged, and how to combine the results of such reconstructions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of the best reconstructions from all images leads to the highest reconstruction quality.

the proposed quality measure is a valuable tool for judging the quality of a reconstruction and the proposed algorithm for combining results is a valuable tool to improve the quality of reconstructions.
the proposed quality measures and the method for combining reconstructions work quite well, but the quality measure is not yet good enough to be the basis for an automatic system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can reconstruct 3D face models from single images of one individual with high quality and in a fully automatic way.

we show that it is possible to reconstruct individual 3D faces from images of one subject, even if the images are of poor quality, and that it is possible for a computer to judge the quality of a reconstruction.
we present a new quality measure for 3D reconstructions that can be used to combine the best of multiple reconstructions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of multiple 3D reconstructions is a promising approach to improve the accuracy of 3D reconstruction.

it is possible to judge the quality of a reconstruction without knowing the ground truth, that it is possible and useful to combine results from different reconstruction algorithms, and that it is possible for a single algorithm to produce results with different quality depending on the image material.
the combination of different quality measures is crucial for a good quality assessment.
